chunks: And Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān narrated from ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

Concerning a man who said, “The first slave I come to own is free,” then he inherited seven all together. He عليه السلام said: “Lots are drawn among them, and the one whose lot comes out is set free.”

key_terms.سَهْمُهُ: his lot or allotted share selected in the draw
key_terms.فَوَرِثَ: then he inherited; came into ownership through inheritance
key_terms.مَمْلُوكٍ: an enslaved person owned as property
key_terms.يُقْرِعُ: he draws lots to determine the applicable case

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone says the first slave he acquires is free, then inherits several slaves at once?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a vowed manumission when multiple slaves come into ownership at the same time through inheritance. In such a case, a lottery is used to determine which one counts as the first owned and is therefore freed.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3395 - Hammad ibn Uthman narrated from Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi, who said that Abu Abdillah (as) said:
"If a man says, 'The first slave I acquire shall be free,' and then he inherits seven slaves altogether, lots are drawn among them, and the one whose lot is drawn shall be freed."
